openwrt_wiki.beschreibung: The NanoPi R2S uses the RK3328 SoC. It has two Gbps Ethernet ports and 1G DDR4 RAM.
openwrt_wiki.hardware_highlights: similar specifications to the discontinued Orange Pi R1 Plus, but has a more expensive ethernet chip compared to the Orange Pi R1 Plus LTS
openwrt_wiki.installation: Uncompress the OpenWrt ...sysupgrade.img.gz image and write it to a micro SD card using a tool like dd or Balena Etcher.
gehaeuse_oeffnen: The all-metal case is held by a single philipps screw.
The plastic (usually yellow) case is held together by clips and can be gently pryed apart with a small flat screwdriver or spudger.
openwrt_wiki.seriell: Connect TX/RX/GND pins of adapter to Debug UART pins on NanoPi R2S board (3 pins near microUSB). The RX and TX pin locations are swapped from some other devices. screen /dev/ttyUSB0 1500000 8N1. Debug UART port is 3.3V TTL. Some USB-TTL adapters ... have trouble operating at 1500000 baud.
openwrt_wiki.hardware_mods: There is a 4 pin fan header which provides 5V at up to 2A of power, depending on the overall power supplied to the R2S.
openwrt_wiki.notes: Ethernet instability can be mitigated by forcing maximum CPU frequency: echo performance > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy0/scaling_governor

oem_bootlog_auszug.kernel: Linux 5.10.60, Machine model: FriendlyElec NanoPi R2S

openwrt_git.installation: Uncompress the OpenWrt sysupgrade and write it to a micro SD card using dd.
openwrt_git.mac: The vendor code supports reading a MAC address from an EEPROM connected via i2c0 of the SoC (address 0x51, offset 0xfa). My two units didn't come with such an EEPROM soldered on (U10). Generating random MAC addresses works around this issue.

openwrt_git_mac.titel: rockchip: use stable MAC-address for NanoPi R2S
openwrt_git_mac.text: The NanoPi R2S does not have a board specific MAC address ... we can use the CID of the used SD card ... to generate the MAC address used for LAN and WAN.
